$comment: [[D-C-DOLLAR-IN-IDENTIFIERS-REFUSED]] runtime witness: `$` starts and continues a C identifier (C23 6.4.2.1 implementation-defined characters). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-22: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (WSL, -std=c2x, -O0 and -O2), MinGW gcc (-std=c2x, -O0 and -O2) and MSVC VS 18 (/std:clatest, /Od and /O2) all BUILD this file and RUN it to 42. Before C's document declared `identifierClass { extraStart "$", extraContinue "$" }`, DSS refused every `$` name with P_IllegalChar.
$commentWhyNotVacuous: Every `$` name is a separate object with its own value and the sum reaches 42 only if each one resolves to itself: a lexer that split `in$ide` into `in` + `$` + `ide`, read `$1` as a number, lost the `#if ON$` arm, or stringized `a$b` as anything but those three bytes changes the exit value or refuses the file. `f$` and the pasted `x$y` have EXTERNAL linkage, so every target's object writer and linker must carry a `$` in a symbol name. ✔MEASURED through dsscp: pe64 runs to 42 natively, elf64-x86_64 in WSL and elf64-aarch64 under qemu, debug and release; macho64-arm64 builds.
